title: Library Management System
description: Design a library system that tracks book inventory, manages member accounts, handles borrowing/returning, computes late fines, and supports reservations for unavailable books. A CRUD-heavy LLD that tests clean entity modeling and rule enforcement.
prompt: Design a library management system where members can borrow and return books, with support for fines and reservations.
prompt_note: Library problems are disarmingly simple-sounding. The trap is under-modeling: most candidates conflate 'Book' (the title) with 'BookItem' (the physical copy). Fix that up front and the design falls into place. Late fines are a natural **Strategy Pattern**, and reservation notifications are a natural **Observer**.

clarifying_questions.question: You: "Can multiple members borrow the same book? I assume the library has multiple physical copies?"
clarifying_questions.answer: Interviewer: "Yes — 'Book' is the title, but there are multiple physical copies ('BookItem' or 'BookCopy') that can be borrowed independently."
clarifying_questions.why: **Critical distinction.** This must be clarified first or the whole design is wrong. Book = metadata; BookItem = loanable physical instance.

clarifying_questions.question: You: "What's the borrowing limit and duration?"
clarifying_questions.answer: Interviewer: "Max 5 books per member, 14-day loan period. Late returns incur a fine per day."
clarifying_questions.why: Business rules to enforce at borrow time. Fine calculation is per overdue day.

clarifying_questions.question: You: "What if a book is fully checked out? Can members reserve it?"
clarifying_questions.answer: Interviewer: "Yes — reservation queue per book. When a copy is returned, notify the first member in the queue."
clarifying_questions.why: Observer Pattern: members subscribe to a book; notified on return. FIFO reservation queue.

clarifying_questions.question: You: "Can members pay fines through the system?"
clarifying_questions.answer: Interviewer: "Mark as paid, yes. Don't integrate a payment gateway."
clarifying_questions.why: Simple state toggle on the fine record.

clarifying_questions.question: You: "Different member types — students, faculty, public — with different limits?"
clarifying_questions.answer: Interviewer: "Yes. Students: 5 books, 14 days. Faculty: 10 books, 30 days. Public: 3 books, 7 days."
clarifying_questions.why: Different borrow policies per member type → **Strategy Pattern** or configuration on Member.

clarifying_questions.question: You: "Search — what can members search by?"
clarifying_questions.answer: Interviewer: "Title, author, genre. Don't build a full-text search engine."
clarifying_questions.why: Simple map-based lookups. Don't over-build the search layer.

core: **Catalog management:** add/remove Books (metadata) and BookItems (physical copies).
**Member management:** register members with type (STUDENT/FACULTY/PUBLIC), each type has different borrow limits.
**Borrow:** member borrows a BookItem → validates (active, under limit, no pending fines) → transitions item to LOANED.
**Return:** member returns a BookItem → compute fine if late → transition to AVAILABLE → notify reservation queue.
**Reservation:** member reserves a Book (all copies checked out) → added to FIFO queue → notified on return.
**Fines:** computed on return based on days overdue × fine rate. Members can pay fines (mark as paid).
**Search:** find books by title, author, genre.
out_of_scope: Full-text search, external ISBN lookup, payment gateway, barcode scanning, multi-branch coordination.

core: **Audit trail:** every borrow/return/reserve is recorded in a loan history.
**Thread-safe operations:** concurrent borrows/returns on the same book must not corrupt inventory.
**Consistent state:** a BookItem can't be simultaneously LOANED to two members.
out_of_scope: Distributed deployment, real-time notifications (we'll just log), high throughput.

primary_scope: `borrowBook(memberId, bookItemId)` → validate → transition item to LOANED → create Loan record
`returnBook(loanId)` → compute fine → transition item to AVAILABLE → notify reservers
termination_points: `BookItemNotAvailableException` — item is LOANED, LOST, or MAINTENANCE
`OutstandingFinesException` — member has unpaid fines (blocked from borrowing)
entity_intro: The critical modeling decision: **Book vs BookItem.** Book holds metadata (title, author, ISBN, genre) shared across all copies. BookItem is a single physical loanable instance with its own barcode, location, and status. Members borrow BookItems, not Books.

entities.name: Book
entities.role: **Model.** Title-level metadata: title, author, ISBN, genre. Immutable reference data. One Book has many BookItems.
entities.verdict_label: ✓ Entity — metadata (many copies share one Book)

entities.name: BookItem
entities.role: **Model.** A physical copy — barcode, rack location, status (AVAILABLE/LOANED/LOST/MAINTENANCE). The loanable unit. State transitions: AVAILABLE → LOANED → AVAILABLE (or LOST on damage).

entities.name: Member
entities.role: **Model.** memberId, name, type (STUDENT/FACULTY/PUBLIC), status (ACTIVE/BLOCKED/EXPIRED), current loan count. Borrow limits derived from type.

entities.name: Loan
entities.role: **Model.** loanId, memberId, bookItemId, borrowedAt, dueDate, returnedAt, fineAmount, status. The borrow transaction record.

entities.name: Reservation
entities.role: **Model.** reservationId, memberId, bookId, createdAt, status. Added to a per-book queue when all items are loaned.

entities.name: Fine
entities.role: **Model.** fineId, loanId, memberId, amount, status (PENDING/PAID). Generated on late return. Blocks further borrowing until paid.

entities.name: BorrowPolicy (Strategy)
entities.role: **Strategy interface.** `getMaxBooks(memberType)`, `getLoanDays(memberType)`, `getFinePerDay(memberType)`. Different values per member type. Could be a simple enum or a full Strategy Pattern — depends on how much variation is expected.

entities.name: LibraryService
entities.role: **Controller.** Public API: borrow, return, reserve, search, payFine. Orchestrates members, books, loans, reservations.

relationships.rel: 1 → N Loans, 1 → N Reservations, 1 → N Fines

relationships.owns: books map, items map, members map, loans map, reservationQueues per book

mvc_note: **MVC Mapping:** **Model** = Book, BookItem, Member, Loan, Reservation, Fine + enums. **Service** = BorrowPolicy (Strategy), FineCalculator. **Controller** = LibraryService (public API, orchestration). The Service layer is thin here — most logic is in the entities themselves (BookItem handles its state transitions, Loan computes its own overdue status).
schema_note: Index `(book_id, created_at)` on reservations for FIFO queue retrieval. Index `due_date` on loans for overdue detection jobs. Index `title` and `author` on books for search.

code_sections.label: Models — Enums + Book + BookItem + Member + Loan
code_sections.flow: **BookItem** is a state machine with `checkOut()` and `checkIn()` transitions — both `synchronized` on the instance to prevent double-loan. **Loan** computes its own `overdueDays()` — encapsulates the business rule. **Member.canBorrow()** checks all the rules: active, under limit, no fines.

code_sections.label: Service — BorrowPolicy (per-type rules)
code_sections.flow: Pure data class mapping member type → borrow rules. Could be a Strategy interface with three implementations, but a single config-style class is simpler for this scope.

code_sections.label: Controller — LibraryService (borrow / return / reserve / fine)
code_sections.flow:
**`borrowBook`:** get member + item → validate canBorrow → `item.checkOut()` → create Loan → increment loan count.
**`returnBook`:** get loan → compute fine if overdue → `item.checkIn()` → mark loan returned → decrement count → **notify reservation queue**.
**`reserveBook`:** add to FIFO queue for that book.
**`payFine`:** toggle status + clear member fines.
code_sections.edge_cases: Borrow with outstanding fine → reject. Borrow at limit → reject. Return same loan twice → guard with status check. Reserve a book you already have → allow (different use case). Member cancels reservation mid-notification → status check.

patterns.name: Strategy Pattern (light) → BorrowPolicy
patterns.why: Different member types have different borrow rules. We could make this a full Strategy interface with three implementations, but the variation is small (just three numbers each), so a config-style class with switch expressions is cleaner. **Rule of thumb:** use full Strategy when behavior varies significantly; use config when only values vary.

patterns.name: Observer Pattern → Reservation Notification
patterns.why: Members subscribe to a book; when an item is returned, the subject (LibraryService on return) notifies the next observer (member at head of reservation queue). The queue is a **FIFO observer list**. Real systems extend this with async email/push delivery — our version just logs.

patterns.name: State Machine → BookItem status
patterns.why: BookItem has a clear state machine: AVAILABLE → LOANED → AVAILABLE (or LOST / MAINTENANCE as alternatives). The `checkOut()` and `checkIn()` methods are the only legal transitions and guard against invalid ones. Encapsulating state transitions inside the entity prevents external code from corrupting state.

concurrency.issue: Two members borrowing the same BookItem simultaneously
concurrency.fix: `BookItem.checkOut()` is `synchronized`. First thread transitions AVAILABLE → LOANED. Second thread sees status != AVAILABLE → throws. Only one wins. This is the **primary race** in a library system, and `synchronized` on the item is sufficient.

concurrency.issue: Borrow and mark-lost race on the same item
concurrency.fix: Both `checkOut()` and `markLost()` are `synchronized` on the BookItem instance. They serialize. The one that acquires the lock first wins — the other sees the new state and handles it (checkOut throws, markLost becomes a no-op on already-lost).

concurrency.issue: Reservation queue race — two members both notified for the same returned item
concurrency.fix: `ConcurrentLinkedQueue.poll()` is atomic — only one member dequeued per call. `notifyNextReserver` is called once per return. If the notified member doesn't borrow the item, they lose their spot; the next return will re-notify the next person.

concurrency.issue: Member's `currentLoanCount` updated concurrently by two borrows
concurrency.fix: `Member.incrementLoanCount()` is `synchronized`. But there's a TOCTOU race: `canBorrow()` check and `incrementLoanCount()` are two steps. A member with limit 5 and 4 current loans could see two concurrent borrows both pass `canBorrow()` → both increment → count becomes 6. **Fix:** make the check-and-increment atomic via a single `synchronized` block in `LibraryService.borrowBook`. Or use an `AtomicInteger` with CAS.

deep_dives.question: Why distinguish Book from BookItem?
deep_dives.answer: **A library has multiple copies of popular books.** 'Book' is a reference data entity (title, author, ISBN) — shared across all copies. 'BookItem' is the loanable physical object with its own barcode, location, and status. You borrow a BookItem, not a Book. Conflating them leads to bugs: 'borrow the book' is ambiguous when there are 5 copies. This is the first modeling decision that separates good from bad library designs.

deep_dives.question: Why isn't BookItem the 'book' entity and Book just a metadata blob on it?
deep_dives.answer: **Reference data normalization.** If you put `title`, `author`, `ISBN` on every BookItem, you'd duplicate that data across copies. Changing an author's name spelling requires updating N rows. With the Book/BookItem split, metadata lives in one place and BookItem is lean. This is **database normalization applied to OOP** — the same principle as 1NF/2NF/3NF.

deep_dives.question: Why is reservation notification synchronous?
deep_dives.answer: **It shouldn't be in production** — notification is a potentially slow operation (email, push, SMS). In our LLD it's a synchronous log statement for simplicity. Production extension: extract a `NotificationService` interface, inject it, and have it enqueue the message in a background queue. The `returnBook` call completes fast; notification happens asynchronously. This is the **Bulkhead + Observer** combination from the Pub/Sub problem.

deep_dives.question: How would you handle a member wanting to hold multiple reserved books?
deep_dives.answer: A member can appear in multiple book queues (one per book they want). Each book has its own FIFO queue. When a book becomes available, the first member in **that book's queue** is notified. No interaction between queues. The only gotcha: if you want to enforce 'max reservations per member,' track it on the Member entity and check on `reserveBook`.

deep_dives.question: How do you handle overdue detection and fine generation at scale?
deep_dives.answer: Two approaches: **(1) On-return:** compute fines only when the book is returned. Simple, but no reminders until return. **(2) Scheduled job:** a daily cron scans active loans with `dueDate < NOW()`, creates/updates Fine records, sends reminder emails. Production libraries do both — reminders from the cron, finalization on return. In a DB: `SELECT * FROM loans WHERE status='ACTIVE' AND due_date < CURRENT_DATE` with an index on `(status, due_date)`.

deep_dives.question: What about lost books — how does the fine work?
deep_dives.answer: Lost books have a different fine model: the member pays the **replacement cost**, not overdue days. Add a `markLost(loanId)` method that: (1) transitions BookItem to LOST, (2) creates a Fine with amount = book's replacement cost, (3) closes the loan. Optionally, the library can set a **lost-book grace period** — the member has 30 days to find it before the replacement fine is finalized.

deep_dives.question: How would you prevent a member from reserving a book they already have checked out?
deep_dives.answer: In `reserveBook()`, check if the member has an active loan for any BookItem of that Book: `loans.values().stream().anyMatch(l -> l.getMemberId().equals(memberId) && l.getStatus() == ACTIVE && getBookFromItem(l.getBarcode()).equals(bookId))`. If yes, either reject (strict mode) or allow (they may want a second copy — unlikely for a library). Business decision.
